title: A Favour of Paint
summary: Ketch is one pigment short of finishing a paint he's been promising himself for thirty years: cairn ochre, the good deep rust-red, stocked by the drowned caretaker's cache cairn. Cairn rule is take one, leave one — so there's a tin of his good tea and a thank-you note to drop in the mail slot first. No clock. Just a long ride and an old man pretending it isn't a big deal.

objectives.label: Take Ketch's consideration tin from the garage bench
Leave the tea and the note in the caretaker's mail slot
Take one charge of cairn ochre — one, not two
Get the pigment back before Ketch's tea goes cold

offer.text: Kid. Favour, not a job — though I'm paying, because favours that touch the road are jobs and anyone who says different is selling something. Thirty years I've been one pigment short of a paint. Cairn ochre, deep rust-red, the kind the drowned crews dug out before I was born. The caretaker stocks it at the cache cairn.

Two rules, and they're the same rule wearing two coats. Take one charge, never two. And leave something for it — the tin on my bench, there's a note inside. That machine keeps a whole field warm for nobody. It gets told thank-you. It gets told by us.

accept.text: Tea to a two-hundred-year-old speaker mast, then grave-goods from a cairn, then home before your tea gets cold. Ketch, this is the most retired-man errand ever run.

Watch it. And mind the walkway at the substation — goes nowhere, stays the right way. You'll see. Oh, and if the caretaker plays you its dawn broadcast, you stand there and *listen*, kid. Some mail you answer by attending.
Substation band. Courier inbound: your business is logged as 'errand, category: paint'. The cache cairn is stocked. The mail slot is oiled. Dusk in forty-one minutes. The lights will be warm.

complete.text: — There it is. Look at that. Rust-red with a violet undertone, like a canyon worrying about something. Two charge-cakes after the Guild fees, cut with bone binder and pan salt, and tomorrow the first coat goes on the mixing-paddle. Twenty-nine years of 'sometime', done by Thursday.
What's it for? Not the Wren — she'd never hide under paint this good. …Ketch. You're grinning. Old man, what is the paint *for*?

For whatever you need it to be for, kid. That's the whole answer and also the honest one. Now clear off — and if the wind out there asks you who mixed it, you say the garage at Saltmouth, and you say it proud. There's a song about bikes like yours, you know. Played it for new riders every season. I'll put it in your book.
